headline: Military budgets swell. Startups scramble. Space remains messy.
deck: This week saw increased military funding alongside startup funding rounds, revealing the complex landscape of space economics.

stories.head: FY27 budget adds $1.4B for space resilience
stories.body: The FY27 budget markup has allocated an additional $1.4 billion to space resilience, signaling a government preference for financial solutions over strategic ones. This funding could enhance capabilities in satellite communications and surveillance, but it also raises questions about the efficiency of spending in a sector often plagued by delays. If only bureaucratic hurdles could be addressed as quickly as cash flows.
stories.soWhat: When the government throws money at a problem, it often leads to more questions than answers—like whether any of this cash will actually result in timely deliveries.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M, valuation hits $1.6B
stories.body: True Anomaly successfully closed a $190 million Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, tapping into the increasing demand for defense-related technologies. With the DoD's growing interest, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on government contracts, but it still faces the challenge of proving its technology in a competitive landscape.
stories.soWhat: A healthy valuation is great, but True Anomaly needs to deliver results, not just promises—especially when Uncle Sam is watching.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team up for SDA bid
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have joined forces for a tactical Space Development Agency constellation bid, showcasing a collaborative approach to defense contracts. This partnership reflects a broader trend in the industry, where companies are increasingly aligning to meet government needs. Given the stakes involved, this could either propel them to success or leave them tangled in red tape.
stories.soWhat: In defense contracting, playing nice is often more effective than going it alone—especially when the government’s attention is on your every move.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's execution
watchlist.body: With $190M in fresh capital, True Anomaly must now demonstrate its capabilities quickly to maintain investor confidence.

watchlist.title: Odin Space's LA office impact
watchlist.body: Odin Space's move to Los Angeles could signal a shift in the orbital debris conversation—Hollywood might not be the only place for drama.

watchlist.title: Watch for Palantir's TITAN integration
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program will be closely monitored for its effectiveness in enhancing military capabilities.

watchlist.title: Anticipate more defense-tech IPOs
watchlist.body: With the defense-tech IPO window slightly ajar, expect more startups to consider going public, potentially reshaping the landscape.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
